page.overview:
Who is Gumar Adraki?

Gumar Adraki was an Andraven villager who lived on the planet Andraven in a village. Around 233 BBY, when it came time to migrate the wellagrin creatures from one side of a mountain to the other, he and his brother Jam were joined by a trio of Jedi younglings: Kai Brightstar, Lys Solay, and Nubs. During their mission, Solay accidentally caused the wellagrins to stampede and bring about an avalanche, splitting up the creatures. The Jedi and villagers split up to reunite the wellagrins, which they successfully did, reaching the top of the mountain. Following another avalanche, the five were able to traverse the falling snow by riding on the wellagrins' backs, landing at the orchard where they planned to take the creatures.

Sometime later, Adraki was in charge of overseeing the annual wellagrin hatching, and the Jedi returned to Andraven to witness it. The process was interrupted and nearly derailed by the businessman Raxlo, whose harvester melted snow near the eggs. Adraki and the Jedi were able to put a stop to the device, saving the baby wellagrins. Later around that year, with the support of his Jedi friends, Adraki later completed the Ancestors Circuit, an Andraven tradition of challenges that everyone in his family had also passed. He planned as much as he could in advance, but unexpected difficulties forced him to think on his feet, which he did successfully. Later, Adraki and the Jedi younglings helped Raxlo reclaim his tenga rock harvesting machine after the Ganguls pirates stole it. On another occasion, Adraki warned Raxlo and the Jedi younglings of a machine harming the wellagrins' habitat.

Gumar Adraki was a male a trio of Jedi younglings—the human Kai Brightstar, the Pantoran Lys Solay, and the Pooba Nubs—visited Andraven during the migration of the wellagrin creatures of the planet. After the Jedi played with the herd for a bit, learning to ride the creatures, Adraki and his younger brother, Jam, were impressed and complimented Solay on her quick learning. Their master, Jedi Master Zia Zanna, then informed them via hologram that they were to accompany the wellagrins on their migration, which Adraki explained was to give them access to more food. The wellagrin trainer, Varna, cautioned them to avoid avalanches, but Adraki assured the younglings that if they stayed with him and Jam, they would be just fine.

The villagers, Adraki sympathized with the difficulty of playing the Andraven flute, encouraging Brightstar that he would get better with practice.
